title: Zero-sum Ramsey numbers of forests and complete bipartite graphs

definitions.name: x2611_14160_subdividedStar
definitions.lean:
def x2611_14160_subdividedStar (a b : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Fin (1 + a + b)) :=
  SimpleGraph.fromRel (fun u v =>
    (u.val = 0 ∧ 1 ≤ v.val ∧ v.val ≤ a) ∨
    (1 ≤ u.val ∧ u.val ≤ b ∧ v.val = a + u.val))
definitions.notes: For a ≥ b: vertex 0 is the center, vertices 1,...,a are its neighbors, and a+i is the extra leaf on arm i for 1 ≤ i ≤ b. SimpleGraph.fromRel symmetrizes the displayed relations. This is the paper’s T_{a,b}.

definitions.name: x2611_14160_copyWeight
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_14160_copyWeight {V W Γ : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [AddCommMonoid Γ] (G : SimpleGraph V) (w : Sym2 W → Γ) (f : V ↪ W) : Γ := by
  classical
  exact ∑ e ∈ G.edgeFinset, w (Sym2.map f e)
definitions.notes: The sum of edge labels of a non-induced copy of G in a complete host, specified by an injective vertex map f. Labels are extended to all Sym2 W; their values on diagonal pairs are never used.

definitions.name: x2611_14160_zeroSumForces
definitions.lean:
def x2611_14160_zeroSumForces {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (m N : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ w : Sym2 (Fin N) → ZMod m, ∃ f : V ↪ Fin N,
    x2611_14160_copyWeight G w f = 0
definitions.notes: Every ZMod m edge labeling of K_N contains a zero-sum (not necessarily induced) copy of G.

definitions.name: x2611_14160_zeroSumRamsey
definitions.notes: The least N with the paper’s zero-sum Ramsey property. The sInf of an empty subset of ℕ is 0; in the claims here the modulus divides the edge count and the usual finite Ramsey argument guarantees existence. The definition also implements the paper’s convention at modulus 1.

definitions.name: x2611_14160_ramsey
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_14160_ramsey {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (r : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {N : ℕ | ∀ w : Sym2 (Fin N) → Fin r,
    ∃ (f : V ↪ Fin N) (c : Fin r),
      ∀ e ∈ G.edgeSet, w (Sym2.map f e) = c}
definitions.notes: Ordinary r-color edge Ramsey number of G with non-induced copies; only r=2 is used. This is not a proper vertex coloring.

definitions.name: x2611_14160_disjointCopies
definitions.notes: The graph tG on pairs (copy index, vertex), with edges only inside a common copy. A zero-sum copy of this graph requires the total packing weight to be zero; its individual components need not each have weight zero.

definitions.name: x2611_14160_cutWeight
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_14160_cutWeight {V Γ : Type*} [Fintype V]
    [AddCommMonoid Γ] (G : SimpleGraph V) (w : Sym2 V → Γ) (A : Finset V) : Γ := by
  classical
  exact ∑ u ∈ A, ∑ v ∈ Finset.univ \ A,
    if G.Adj u v then w (Sym2.mk u v) else 0
definitions.notes: The weight of δ_G(A). Summing from A to its complement counts every crossing edge exactly once. All graphs considered are finite, as in the introduction.

definitions.name: x2611_14160_twoGroupD
definitions.lean:
def x2611_14160_twoGroupD {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] (a : ι → ℕ) : ℕ :=
  1 + ∑ i, (2 ^ a i - 1)
definitions.notes: D(Γ) for a presentation Γ = ∏ i, ZMod (2^(a i)), with positive exponents. A finite direct product is the same as the paper’s finite direct sum. The empty index type gives the trivial group and D=1.

definitions.name: x2611_14160_twoGroupCondition
definitions.lean:
def x2611_14160_twoGroupCondition (Γ : Type*) [AddCommGroup Γ] (q : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (s : ℕ) (a : Fin s → ℕ), (∀ i, 1 ≤ a i) ∧
    Nonempty (Γ ≃+ ((i : Fin s) → ZMod (2 ^ a i))) ∧
    x2611_14160_twoGroupD a ≤ q
definitions.notes: The condition “Γ is a finite abelian 2-group with D(Γ) ≤ q”, expressed by existence of a cyclic decomposition. It includes the empty decomposition of the trivial group. This avoids choosing a decomposition or defining D for non-2-groups.

definitions.name: x2611_14160_obstructionLabel
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_14160_obstructionLabel (a s m : ℕ) :
    Sym2 (Fin (2 * (a - 1) + s)) → ZMod m := by
  classical
  exact fun e =>
    if ∃ v ∈ e.toFinset, 2 * (a - 1) ≤ v.val then 1
    else if (∃ v ∈ e.toFinset, v.val < a - 1) ∧
      (∃ v ∈ e.toFinset, a - 1 ≤ v.val ∧ v.val < 2 * (a - 1))
    then -1 else 0
definitions.notes: Figure 2 / Lemma 2.1 labeling: P consists of the first a−1 vertices, Q of the next a−1, X of the final s. Edges meeting X get +1, P–Q edges get −1, and all other edges get 0, in ZMod m.

definitions.name: x2611_14160_forestRatios
definitions.notes: Ratios over all finite forests with m edges, allowing isolated vertices as printed. Theorem 1.3 represents the printed maximum by a function whose value is IsGreatest in this set, rather than silently replacing a maximum by a supremum.

definitions.name: x2611_14160_defect
definitions.lean:
noncomputable def x2611_14160_defect {V : Type*} [Fintype V]
    (G : SimpleGraph V) (t : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sInf {d : ℕ | ∀ w : Sym2 (Fin (2 * Fintype.card V)) → ZMod t,
    (∀ f : V ↪ Fin (2 * Fintype.card V),
      ∃ g : V ↪ Fin (2 * Fintype.card V),
        Disjoint (Set.range f) (Set.range g) ∧
        x2611_14160_copyWeight G w f = x2611_14160_copyWeight G w g) ∨
    (∃ S : Finset (Fin (2 * Fintype.card V)), S.card ≤ Fintype.card V + d ∧
      ∃ f g : V ↪ Fin (2 * Fintype.card V),
        Set.range f ⊆ (S : Set (Fin (2 * Fintype.card V))) ∧
        Set.range g ⊆ (S : Set (Fin (2 * Fintype.card V))) ∧
        x2611_14160_copyWeight G w f ≠ x2611_14160_copyWeight G w g)}
definitions.notes: Definition 3.6 verbatim in content: the least nonnegative d such that each labeling of K_{2n} has either disjoint equal-weight partners for every copy, or two different-weight copies on a common set of at most n+d vertices. All copies are injective maps into the complete host.

statements.label: Theorem 1.3
statements.name: x2611_14160_thm1_3
statements.original:
For every positive integer $k$ , put $T_{k}=T_{276k,12k}$ . Then

 $e(T_{k})=288k,\qquad R(T_{k},2)\leq 553k,\qquad R(T_{k},\mathbb{Z}_{288k})\geq 554k-1.$ 

Consequently

 $\liminf_{k\to\infty}\frac{R(T_{k},\mathbb{Z}_{288k})}{R(T_{k},2)}\geq\frac{554}{553}>1.$ 

Moreover, for every integer $m\geq 576$ there is a tree $T$ with $e(T)=m$ 
and $R(T,\mathbb{Z}_{m})>R(T,2)$ , and

 $\liminf_{m\to\infty}\max_{\begin{subarray}{c}F\text{ a forest}\\
e(F)=m\end{subarray}}\frac{R(F,\mathbb{Z}_{m})}{R(F,2)}\geq\frac{554}{553}>1.$ 

In particular, Conjecture 1.1 is false.

    554*k-1 ≤ x2611_14160_zeroSumRamsey (x2611_14160_subdividedStar (276*k) (12*k)) (288*k)) ∧

statements.label: Theorem 1.4
statements.name: x2611_14160_thm1_4
statements.original:
Let $q\geq 2$ be a power of two and $s,k\geq 1$ . Then

 $R(K_{s,kq},\mathbb{Z}_{q})=s+kq\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad s\geq q\ \text{ or }\ q-s\in\{2^{j}:j\geq 0\}.$ 

For $q\geq 4$ , the least $s_{0}$ for which equality holds for every
 $k\geq 1$ and every $s\geq s_{0}$ is $q-2$ . For every $m\geq 2$ ,

 $R(mK_{q,q},\mathbb{Z}_{m})=2qm+\frac{m}{\gcd(m,q)}-1.$

      q ≤ s ∨ ∃ j : ℕ, q-s = 2^j)) ∧
  (4 ≤ q → IsLeast {s₀ : ℕ | 1 ≤ s₀ ∧ ∀ k s : ℕ, 1 ≤ k → s₀ ≤ s →
    x2611_14160_zeroSumRamsey (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin s) (Fin (k*q))) q = s+k*q}
    (q-2)) ∧

    (x2611_14160_disjointCopies m (completeBipartiteGraph (Fin q) (Fin q))) m =
    2*q*m + m / Nat.gcd m q - 1)

statements.label: Lemma 2.1(i)
statements.name: x2611_14160_lem2_1_i
statements.original:
Let $a>b\geq 1$ and $s\geq 1$ be integers.

(i) 

If $6s\leq b+1$ , then

 $R(T_{a,b},\mathbb{Z}_{a+b})\geq 2a+s-1.$ 

More generally, let $T$ be a tree with $m$ edges and bipartition sizes
 $t_{1}\leq t_{2}$ , let $L,s\geq 1$ , and suppose that for some vertex $c$ each
component of $T-c$ has at most $L$ vertices and that $T-c$ contains a
matching of size $s$ . If

 $\deg_{T}(c)>m/2\qquad\text{and}\qquad L(L+1)s\leq t_{1},$ 

then $R(T,\mathbb{Z}_{m})\geq 2t_{2}+s-1$ .
statements.lean:

    2*a+s-1 ≤ x2611_14160_zeroSumRamsey (x2611_14160_subdividedStar a b) (a+b)) ∧
  (∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] (T : SimpleGraph V) (m t₁ t₂ L s : ℕ)
    (B₁ B₂ : Finset V) (c : V),
    T.IsTree → Nat.card T.edgeSet = m → t₁ ≤ t₂ →
    T.IsBipartiteWith (B₁ : Set V) (B₂ : Set V) →
    (B₁ : Set V) ∪ (B₂ : Set V) = Set.univ → B₁.card = t₁ → B₂.card = t₂ →
    1 ≤ L → 1 ≤ s →
    (∀ C : (T.induce {v : V | v ≠ c}).ConnectedComponent, Nat.card C.supp ≤ L) →
    (∃ M : (T.induce {v : V | v ≠ c}).Subgraph, M.IsMatching ∧ Nat.card M.edgeSet = s) →
    m < 2 * Nat.card (T.neighborSet c) → L*(L+1)*s ≤ t₁ →
    2*t₂+s-1 ≤ x2611_14160_zeroSumRamsey T m)
statements.notes: Includes both the subdivided-star inequality and its printed generalization. The two finsets form the full bipartition, with t₁ ≤ t₂. T−c is the induced graph on vertices unequal to c. Component size counts vertices; matching size counts edges. The strict inequality m < 2 deg(c) is exactly deg(c)>m/2, without natural-number division ambiguity.

statements.name: x2611_14160_lem2_5

statements.label: Lemma 3.1
statements.name: x2611_14160_lem3_1
statements.original:
Let $q\geq 2$ be a power of two and $\Gamma$ a finite abelian $2$ -group
with $D(\Gamma)\leq q$ . Let $t$ be a positive multiple of $q$ , and let
 $D(\Gamma)\leq h\leq q$ . For any $\Gamma$ -labeling $w$ of the edges of a graph
 $G$ and any $W\subseteq V(G)$ of size $t+h-1$ , an odd number of
 $t$ -subsets $A$ of $W$ satisfy $w(\delta_{G}(A))=0$ , and an even
number give each other weight. The minimum size $t+D(\Gamma)-1$ of $W$ 
in this assertion is sharp for guaranteeing a zero-weight cut with
the chosen $t$ -set contained in $W$ .

statements.label: Lemma 3.2
statements.name: x2611_14160_lem3_2
statements.original:
Let $q\geq 2$ be a power of two, and let $\Gamma$ be a finite abelian group.
Every $\Gamma$ -labeling of $E(K_{2q})$ contains a zero-sum $K_{q,q}$ if
and only if $\Gamma$ is a $2$ -group with $D(\Gamma)\leq q$ . Whenever this
condition holds, the number of unordered balanced cuts of weight
zero is odd, and the number of each other weight is even.

  (Γ : Type) [AddCommGroup Γ] [Fintype Γ] :
  ((∀ w : Sym2 (Fin (2*q)) → Γ, ∃ A : Finset (Fin (2*q)), A.card = q ∧
    x2611_14160_cutWeight (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2*q))) w A = 0) ↔
    x2611_14160_twoGroupCondition Γ q) ∧
  (x2611_14160_twoGroupCondition Γ q →
    ∀ (w : Sym2 (Fin (2*q)) → Γ) (v : Fin (2*q)) (g : Γ),
    (g = 0 → Odd (Nat.card {A : Finset (Fin (2*q)) // A.card = q ∧ v ∉ A ∧
      x2611_14160_cutWeight (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (2*q))) w A = g})) ∧

statements.notes: The iff ranges over all labelings of K_{2q}. twoGroupCondition is exactly the cyclic-decomposition condition “2-group and D≤q”. For the parity assertion, fixing any vertex v and taking the side avoiding v gives one representative of each unordered balanced cut; there is no extra factor of two.

statements.label: Lemma 3.3 (general group spanning assertions)
statements.name: x2611_14160_lem3_3
statements.original:
Let $q\geq 2$ be a power of two and let $\Gamma$ be a finite abelian
 $2$ -group with $D(\Gamma)\leq q$ . If $k,s\geq 1$ and $s\geq D(\Gamma)-1$ , then
every $\Gamma$ -labeling of $K_{kq+s}$ contains a spanning zero-sum copy
of $K_{kq,s}$ . The same conclusion holds when $1\leq s<q$ and
 $q-s$ is a power of two, including $1$ .
statements.lean:
(ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (a : ι → ℕ) (ha : ∀ i, 1 ≤ a i)
  (q k s : ℕ) (hq : 2 ≤ q) (hpow : ∃ b : ℕ, q = 2^b)
  (hD : x2611_14160_twoGroupD a ≤ q) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hs : 1 ≤ s)
  (hsize : x2611_14160_twoGroupD a - 1 ≤ s ∨
    (s < q ∧ ∃ j : ℕ, q-s = 2^j)) :
  ∀ w : Sym2 (Fin (k*q+s)) → ((i : ι) → ZMod (2^a i)),
    ∃ A : Finset (Fin (k*q+s)), A.card = k*q ∧
      x2611_14160_cutWeight (⊤ : SimpleGraph (Fin (k*q+s))) w A = 0
statements.notes: Formalizes the first paragraph, including both sufficient conditions. The group is given by its cyclic presentation, as in Lemma 3.1. A kq-set in a host of kq+s vertices has complement of size s, so its zero cut is exactly a spanning zero-sum K_{kq,s}. The subsequent cyclic iff and least-threshold clauses are already retained in Theorem 1.4.

statements.label: Remark 3.4 (Odd prime moduli)
statements.name: x2611_14160_remark3_4
statements.original:
The hypothesis that $q$ is a power of two cannot be removed: for every
odd prime $p$ one has $R(K_{p,p},\mathbb{Z}_{p})\geq 2p+1$ .

statements.label: Section 3.3 (counterexample family and q=4)
statements.name: x2611_14160_counterexamples
statements.original:
In particular, for every power of two $q\geq 2$ , taking $m=2q$ gives

 $R(2qK_{q,q},\mathbb{Z}_{2q})=4q^{2}+1,\qquad\operatorname{def}_{2q}(K_{q,q})=1.$ 

The conjectured value is $4q^{2}+2q-1$ , so the exact gap is $2q-2>0$ .
As explained in Remark 1.5, the failure of the
conjecture for this family already follows from the earlier results
of Caro and Caro–Provstgaard. For $q=4$ , the exact value
 $R(8K_{4,4},\mathbb{Z}_{8})=65$ sharpens their upper bound $67$ ; the
conjectured value is $71$ .
